text:
Response A is better: it is accurate, within the word limit, and gives the manager a clear takeaway.

**Accuracy:** Both responses report the figures correctly (214 workers, 31% vs 44%, 47 to 19 minutes, 78%). Response A frames the 78% as perceived productivity ("*felt* more productive") set against the null measured result. Response B lists the 78% under "Benefits found", which could mislead a skimming reader into treating it as a real benefit. Response A also correctly describes the standing-time drop as a fade in novelty.

**Length:** Response A is about 100 words, inside the 120-word limit. Response B is about 145 words, so it breaks the explicit constraint. Much of the excess is filler ("It is worth noting that", "There are also a few points to keep in mind").

**Useful content:** Response A includes a practical implication (justify the desks on comfort and health, not productivity). Response B leaves the manager to work that out.

Verdict: A
